title: Quapaw language — Grokipedia
text: The Quapaw people, whose language belongs to the Dhegiha branch of the Siouan family, trace their ancestral origins to the Ohio River Valley, where their Dhegiha-speaking forebears lived near the confluence of the Ohio and Wabash Rivers around the time of European contact.

title: Quapaw Language - Sam Noble Museum
text: The Quapaw language was originally spoken in southeastern Arkansas in the area where the Arkansas River meets the Mississippi River. Quapaw is a member of the Dhegiha branch of the Siouan-Catawban language family.
